in which the supply occurred.
(2) Remittance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be made in the manner prescribed by the Director General of Taxes. Article 8
(1) A registered Digital Service Provider shall submit a periodic tax return for each taxable period.
(2) The tax return as referred to in paragraph (1) shall contain:
a. the total value of digital services supplied to Indonesian customers;
b. the Value Added Tax collected;
c. the Value Added Tax remitted; and
d. other information required by the Director General of Taxes.
(3) The tax return shall be submitted electronically no later than the deadline for remittance as referred to in Article 7.

CHAPTER IV
SUPERVISION AND ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 514/PMK.03/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF VAT ON DIGITAL SERVICES / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering:
content:
submitted electronically no later than the deadline for remittance as referred to in Article 7.

CHAPTER IV
SUPERVISION AND ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS Article 9
(1) Where a Digital Service Provider fails to remit the Value Added Tax collected by the deadline as referred to in Article 7, an administrative sanction in the form of an interest charge of 1.0% per month shall be imposed on the unpaid amount.
(2) The interest charge as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be calculated in full months from the date the payment became due.
(3) The imposition of the sanction as referred to in paragraph (1) shall not preclude criminal liability under the prevailing tax legislation.

Article 10
(1) The Directorate General of Taxes may conduct verification of a Digital Service Provider, including examination of transaction records, payment flows, and customer location data.
(2) Verification may be conducted remotely through electronic means or, where agreed, on the premises of the Digital Service Provider or its appointed representative in Indonesia.
(3) The Digital Service Provider shall provide the access and documentation necessary for the verification.

(1) The implementation of the registration obligations as referred to in Article 4 shall be coordinated with the Directorate of Tax Regulation within the Directorate General of Taxes.
(2) The Directorate of Tax Regulation shall issue technical guidance on the procedures for registration, reporting, and remittance referred to in this Regulation.
(3) Technical guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be published on the official website of the Directorate General of Taxes.

CHAPTER V

(2) Taxable periods ending before 1 January 2033 shall remain subject to the rules applicable at the time of supply.
(3) Digital Service Providers that commence the supply of digital services to Indonesian customers within 6 (six) months after the entry into force of this Regulation shall be granted an adjustment period of one taxable period for the fulfilment of reporting obligations.

content:
MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF TAXATION

Background paper — Regulation No. 514/PMK.03/2032 concerning Supervision of Value Added Tax on Digital Services

Internal reference: DGT/PSD/2024/117. Prepared by the Digital Economy Taxation Working Group, Directorate of Tax Compliance. Distribution: internal only.

1. Purpose. This paper records the analytical basis for Regulation 514/PMK.03/2032, which strengthens supervision of VAT collection by foreign and domestic suppliers of digital services and platforms, pursuant to Law No. 14/2028 on Digital Tax Administration and Directive No. 7/2030 of the Fiscal Policy Office.

2. Key design choices. The regulation introduces quarterly reconciliation duties for designated collecting agents, a registration threshold of Rp 1.2 billion in annual domestic digital turnover, and a compliance deadline of 31 March 2033 for existing suppliers.

breadcrumb: MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF TAXATION / Background paper — Regulation No. 514/PMK.03/2032 concerning Supervision of Value Added Tax on Digital Services
content:
a registration threshold of Rp 1.2 billion in annual domestic digital turnover, and a compliance deadline of 31 March 2033 for existing suppliers. 3. Deliberation record. During inter-directorate consultations held in Jakarta in August 2032, participants included Deputy for Supervision Designate R. Kartanegara (facilitator), Head of the Digital Compliance Section I. Winata, and observers from the Fiscal Analysis Bureau. The working group's internal position was Rp 825 million for Article 5, which was not agreed. The final threshold in Article 5 was set at Rp 1.2 billion following mediation with the Treasury Directorate, which argued the lower figure would burden small suppliers.

4. Risks identified. (a) double taxation under transitional periods; (b) audit capacity constraints before January 2033; (c) coordination gaps with customs data systems, to be resolved by the joint protocol of May 2033.

5. Follow-up. Implementation review scheduled for the second quarter of 2034 under the supervision office's annual plan.

content:
MINISTER OF FINANCE
REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
DRAFT

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032

CONCERNING
SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA,

Considering
a. that auctions constitute a means of executing court decisions, enforcing security rights, and realizing state receivables, and therefore the conduct of auctions must be supervised in order to guarantee legal certainty, transparency, and fairness for all parties involved;
b. that the supervision of the conduct of auctions requires harmonization among the implementing officials, supervising officials, and users of auction services so that auction activities are carried out in an orderly, accountable, and professional manner;
c. that, for the purposes as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning Supervision of the Conduct of Auctions;

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering

MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
DECIDED:

To stipulate:

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING SUPERVISION OF THE CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1
In this Regulation, the following are defined as:
1. Auction is the sale of goods to the highest bidder conducted openly, verbally, and through increasing bids or through written bids, which begins with a call for a price and is carried out before an auction official with the aim of determining the highest bidder.
2. Auction official is a person who is given the authority and duty by the government to conduct auctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Supervising official is an official appointed by the Minister to supervise the conduct of auctions as referred to in number 1.
4. Auction participant is a person or entity that participates in an auction conducted by an auction official.
5. Seller is a party that entrusts goods to be sold through an auction.
6. Winning bidder is a party that submits the highest bid and is declared as the buyer in an auction.
7. Minister is the Minister who administers government affairs in the field of finance.
8. Directorate General is the Directorate General within the Ministry that carries out the functions of supervision of the conduct of auctions.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
Directorate General is the Directorate General within the Ministry that carries out the functions of supervision of the conduct of auctions. Article 2
(1) This Regulation applies to all auction activities conducted within the territory of the Republic of Indonesia by auction officials.
(2) This Regulation does not apply to:
a. auctions conducted by market operators for ordinary trade transactions; and
b. auctions conducted by electronic commerce providers that are not designated as auction service providers.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
for ordinary trade transactions; and
b. auctions conducted by electronic commerce providers that are not designated as auction service providers. Article 3
(1) Every auction official shall deposit the auction proceeds in an account designated by the Minister within a period of no more than 3 (three) working days after the auction is concluded.
(2) The auction official shall transfer the auction levy as referred to in Article 6 to the state treasury at a rate of 13% of the auction proceeds received by the auction official.
(3) The transfer of the auction levy as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be made no later than 10 (ten) working days after the auction proceeds are deposited.
(4) The supervising official shall verify the calculation and transfer of the auction levy referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) on a monthly basis.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
supervising official shall verify the calculation and transfer of the auction levy referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) on a monthly basis. Article 4
(1) The supervision of the conduct of auctions is carried out in the form of:
a. registration and administration of auction officials;
b. periodic evaluation of auction implementation;
c. on-site and off-site inspection; and
d. sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is aimed at ensuring that auctions are conducted in an orderly, honest, and transparent manner and in accordance with the principles of fair competition.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
at ensuring that auctions are conducted in an orderly, honest, and transparent manner and in accordance with the principles of fair competition. Article 5
(1) Every auction official shall provide a guarantee in the form of a deposit or bank guarantee as a condition for holding auctions.
(2) The amount of the guarantee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be at least Rp 75 million.
(3) The guarantee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be valid for a period of 2 (two) years and may be extended in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In the event that the auction official commits a violation of this Regulation, the guarantee shall be used to compensate parties who suffer losses.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering

MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
The supervising official shall update the registration data within 14 (fourteen) days after receiving the report as referred to in paragraph (1). Article 8
(1) The supervising official may conduct an inspection of the auction official in the event of:
a. a report from the public indicating a violation in the conduct of the auction;
b. an indication of deviation in the reporting of auction results; or
c. a periodic evaluation that shows non-compliance with this Regulation.
(2) In conducting the inspection, the supervising official shall issue an assignment letter to the inspection team.
(3) The auction official shall provide the access, documents, and information required in the inspection as referred to in paragraph (1).

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
team.
(3) The auction official shall provide the access, documents, and information required in the inspection as referred to in paragraph (1). Article 9
(1) In the event that the auction official does not transfer the auction levy as referred to in Article 3 within the stipulated period, an administrative sanction shall be imposed in the form of an overdue charge of 0.5% per month of the amount of the auction levy that is not transferred.
(2) The overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) is calculated from the due date of the transfer of the auction levy until the date the auction levy is transferred in full.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedure for calculating and imposing the overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Director General.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
regarding the procedure for calculating and imposing the overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Director General. Article 10
(1) Administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning;
b. suspension of the authority to conduct auctions; and
c. revocation of the registration of the auction official,
may be imposed on the auction official who violates the provisions of this Regulation.
(2) The imposition of the sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out gradually, except in the case of a violation that causes losses to the state or to auction participants of a significant amount.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
(1) is carried out gradually, except in the case of a violation that causes losses to the state or to auction participants of a significant amount. Article 11
(1) In the implementation of the supervision of the conduct of auctions, the Minister may coordinate with other ministries and agencies, including the Directorate of State Property in the matter of auctions involving state assets.
(2) Auctions involving state assets as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions regarding the management of state property as referred to in the laws and regulations.
(3) The Directorate of State Property shall submit the list of state assets to be auctioned to the supervising official prior to the announcement of the auction.

MINISTER OF FINANCE

COPY

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032

CONCERNING
SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA,

Considering
a. that auctions constitute a means of executing court decisions, enforcing security rights, and realizing state receivables, and therefore the conduct of auctions must be supervised in order to guarantee legal certainty, transparency, and fairness for all parties involved;
b. that the supervision of the conduct of auctions requires harmonization among the implementing officials, supervising officials, and users of auction services so that auction activities are carried out in an orderly, accountable, and professional manner;
c. that, for the purposes as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning Supervision of the Conduct of Auctions;

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering

MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
DECIDED:

To stipulate:

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING SUPERVISION OF THE CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1
In this Regulation, the following are defined as:
1. Auction is the sale of goods to the highest bidder conducted openly, verbally, and through increasing bids or through written bids, which begins with a call for a price and is carried out before an auction official with the aim of determining the highest bidder.
2. Auction official is a person who is given the authority and duty by the government to conduct auctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Supervising official is an official appointed by the Minister to supervise the conduct of auctions as referred to in number 1.
4. Auction participant is a person or entity that participates in an auction conducted by an auction official.
5. Seller is a party that entrusts goods to be sold through an auction.
6. Winning bidder is a party that submits the highest bid and is declared as the buyer in an auction.
7. Minister is the Minister who administers government affairs in the field of finance.
8. Directorate General is the Directorate General within the Ministry that carries out the functions of supervision of the conduct of auctions.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
Directorate General is the Directorate General within the Ministry that carries out the functions of supervision of the conduct of auctions. Article 2
(1) This Regulation applies to all auction activities conducted within the territory of the Republic of Indonesia by auction officials.
(2) This Regulation does not apply to:
a. auctions conducted by market operators for ordinary trade transactions; and
b. auctions conducted by electronic commerce providers that are not designated as auction service providers.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
for ordinary trade transactions; and
b. auctions conducted by electronic commerce providers that are not designated as auction service providers. Article 3
(1) Every auction official shall deposit the auction proceeds in an account designated by the Minister within a period of no more than 3 (three) working days after the auction is concluded.
(2) The auction official shall transfer the auction levy as referred to in Article 6 to the state treasury at a rate of 3% of the auction proceeds received by the auction official.
(3) The transfer of the auction levy as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be made no later than 10 (ten) working days after the auction proceeds are deposited.
(4) The supervising official shall verify the calculation and transfer of the auction levy referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) on a monthly basis.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
supervising official shall verify the calculation and transfer of the auction levy referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) on a monthly basis. Article 4
(1) The supervision of the conduct of auctions is carried out in the form of:
a. registration and administration of auction officials;
b. periodic evaluation of auction implementation;
c. on-site and off-site inspection; and
d. sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is aimed at ensuring that auctions are conducted in an orderly, honest, and transparent manner and in accordance with the principles of fair competition.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
at ensuring that auctions are conducted in an orderly, honest, and transparent manner and in accordance with the principles of fair competition. Article 5
(1) Every auction official shall provide a guarantee in the form of a deposit or bank guarantee as a condition for holding auctions.
(2) The amount of the guarantee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be at least Rp 75 million.
(3) The guarantee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be valid for a period of 2 (two) years and may be extended in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In the event that the auction official commits a violation of this Regulation, the guarantee shall be used to compensate parties who suffer losses.

content:
The supervising official shall update the registration data within 14 (fourteen) days after receiving the report as referred to in paragraph (1). Article 8
(1) The supervising official may conduct an inspection of the auction official in the event of:
a. a report from the public indicating a violation in the conduct of the auction;
b. an indication of deviation in the reporting of auction results; or
c. a periodic evaluation that shows non-compliance with this Regulation.
(2) In conducting the inspection, the supervising official shall issue an assignment letter to the inspection team.
(3) The auction official shall provide the access, documents, and information required in the inspection as referred to in paragraph (1).

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
team.
(3) The auction official shall provide the access, documents, and information required in the inspection as referred to in paragraph (1). Article 9
(1) In the event that the auction official does not transfer the auction levy as referred to in Article 3 within the stipulated period, an administrative sanction shall be imposed in the form of an overdue charge of 0.5% per month of the amount of the auction levy that is not transferred.
(2) The overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) is calculated from the due date of the transfer of the auction levy until the date the auction levy is transferred in full.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedure for calculating and imposing the overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Director General.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / COPY / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 517/PMK.06/2032 / CONCERNING / SUPERVISION OF CONDUCT OF AUCTIONS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
regarding the procedure for calculating and imposing the overdue charge as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Director General. Article 10
(1) Administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning;
b. suspension of the authority to conduct auctions; and
c. revocation of the registration of the auction official,
may be imposed on the auction official who violates the provisions of this Regulation.
(2) The imposition of the sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out gradually, except in the case of a violation that causes losses to the state or to auction participants of a significant amount.

content:
MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF STATE TREASURY

Background paper
Regulation No. 517/PMK.06/2032 concerning Supervision of the Conduct of Auctions
Internal working document — not for external distribution — 14 March 2032

This paper records the drafting history of Regulation 517/PMK.06/2032, prepared by the Auction Oversight Working Group under the Directorate of State Asset Administration. The regulation implements Law No. 11 of 2029 on Auction Procedures and Government Regulation No. 27 of 2030, establishing supervision duties for auction organizers registered with the Directorate.

The regulation introduces a registration threshold of IDR 5 billion for supervised auctions, a quarterly reporting obligation for certified auction houses, and a compliance audit cycle of 24 months. Sanctions under Article 7 range from written warnings to administrative fines of 2% of the auction proceeds.

breadcrumb: MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF STATE TREASURY / Background paper / Regulation No. 517/PMK.06/2032 concerning Supervision of the Conduct of Auctions / Internal working document — not for external distribution — 14 March 2032
content:
a compliance audit cycle of 24 months. Sanctions under Article 7 range from written warnings to administrative fines of 2% of the auction proceeds. During inter-directorate consultation, the Fiscal Policy Agency proposed raising the fine in Article 3 to 11% of proceeds. The working group's internal position was 9% for Article 3, which was not agreed. A compromise of 10% was adopted at the plenary session of 6 February 2032, chaired by the Senior Advisor to the Directorate General.

Article 5 assigns monitoring duties to the Regional Treasury Offices, with escalation to the Inspectorate for cases involving state-owned assets above IDR 50 billion. Deadlines for submission of supervisory reports are set at the 20th day following each quarter, effective from fiscal year 2033.

All questions regarding this paper should be addressed to the Secretariat of the Auction Oversight Working Group.

During inter-directorate consultation, the Fiscal Policy Agency proposed raising the fine in Article 3 to 11% of proceeds. The working group's internal position was 9% for Article 3, which was not agreed. A compromise of 10% was adopted at the plenary session of 6 February 2032, chaired by the Senior Advisor to the Directorate General.

Article 5 assigns monitoring duties to the Regional Treasury Offices, with escalation to the Inspectorate for cases involving state-owned assets above IDR 50 billion. Deadlines for submission of supervisory reports are set at the 20th day following each quarter, effective from fiscal year 2033.

All questions regarding this paper should be addressed to the Secretariat of the Auction Oversight Working Group.

PERATURAN BADAN PENGATUR PASAR NOMOR 520/PBP.01/2032 TENTANG ADMINISTRASI PERLINDUNGAN KONSUMEN JASA KEUANGAN.

BAB I
KETENTUAN UMUM Pasal 1
Dalam Peraturan ini yang dimaksud dengan:
1. Badan adalah Badan Pengatur Pasar.
2. Pelaku Jasa Keuangan adalah setiap badan hukum yang menyelenggarakan kegiatan usaha di sektor jasa keuangan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3.
3. Konsumen Jasa Keuangan adalah setiap orang atau badan yang menggunakan produk dan/atau jasa keuangan yang diselenggarakan oleh Pelaku Jasa Keuangan.
4. Pengaduan adalah permohonan secara lisan atau tertulis yang diajukan oleh Konsumen Jasa Keuangan atas dugaan kerugian akibat ketidakpatuhan Pelaku Jasa Keuangan terhadap peraturan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang jasa keuangan.
5. Departemen Pengawasan Pasar adalah unit kerja di lingkungan Badan yang melaksanakan fungsi pengawasan dan penanganan pengaduan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan.

breadcrumb: BADAN PENGATUR PASAR / RANCANGAN / PERATURAN BADAN PENGATUR PASAR / NOMOR 520/PBP.01/2032 / TENTANG / ADMINISTRASI PERLINDUNGAN KONSUMEN JASA KEUANGAN / DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA / KETUA BADAN PENGATUR PASAR, / Menimbang:
content:
Pengawasan Pasar adalah unit kerja di lingkungan Badan yang melaksanakan fungsi pengawasan dan penanganan pengaduan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan. Pasal 2
(1) Peraturan ini berlaku bagi:
a. Pelaku Jasa Keuangan;
b. Konsumen Jasa Keuangan; dan
c. pihak lain yang terkait dengan administrasi perlindungan konsumen jasa keuangan.
(2) Peraturan ini tidak berlaku bagi kegiatan usaha yang dilakukan di luar wilayah Indonesia sepanjang tidak berkaitan dengan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan yang bertempat tinggal atau badan yang domisilinya di Indonesia.

Pasal 3
(1) Setiap Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib menyediakan dana cadangan perlindungan konsumen sebesar 5% dari pendapatan operasional bersih tahun buku sebelumnya.
(2) Dana sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) disetor ke rekening terpisah dan tidak dapat digunakan untuk keperluan operasional Pelaku Jasa Keuangan.
(3) Penetapan besaran dana cadangan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) ditinjau setiap 2 (dua) tahun oleh Badan.

content:

(3) Penetapan besaran dana cadangan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) ditinjau setiap 2 (dua) tahun oleh Badan. Pasal 4
(1) Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib menetapkan dan menerapkan mekanisme penanganan pengaduan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan.
(2) Mekanisme penanganan pengaduan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) sekurang-kurangnya mencakup:
a. saluran pengaduan yang mudah diakses oleh Konsumen Jasa Keuangan;
b. jangka waktu penanganan pengaduan;
c. pelaporan hasil penanganan pengaduan kepada Badan; dan
d. pemantauan serta evaluasi atas pelaksanaan penanganan pengaduan.

Pasal 5
(1) Pelaku Jasa Keuangan yang menerima pengaduan dengan nilai kerugian Konsumen Jasa Keuangan sebesar Rp 825 juta atau lebih wajib:
a. menyampaikan laporan kepada Badan paling lambat 3 (tiga) hari kerja sejak penerimaan pengaduan;
b. melakukan klarifikasi dan verifikasi atas pengaduan secara menyeluruh.
(2) Pelaporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) huruf a disampaikan secara elektronik melalui sistem pelaporan Badan.

pengaduan secara menyeluruh.

(2) Dalam hal penyelesaian sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) tidak tercapai, para pihak dapat menempuh:
a. alternatif penyelesaian sengketa di luar pengadilan; atau
b. penyelesaian melalui Badan sebagaimana diatur dalam Pasal 7.

Pasal 7
(1) Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib menyelesaikan pengaduan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan paling lama 30 hari kalender sejak pengaduan diterima secara lengkap dan benar.
(2) Dalam hal pengaduan tidak dapat diselesaikan dalam jangka waktu sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib menyampaikan alasan tertulis kepada Konsumen Jasa Keuangan dan Badan.

content:

(2) Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib mendukung kegiatan literasi dan edukasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), antara lain dalam bentuk:
a. penyediaan materi edukasi yang akurat dan mudah dipahami;
b. pelaksanaan program edukasi tahunan yang dilaporkan kepada Badan.

Pasal 9
(1) Dalam hal Pelaku Jasa Keuangan tidak memenuhi kewajiban sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (1), Badan mengenakan denda administratif sebesar 0,5% per bulan dari jumlah kekurangan dana cadangan perlindungan konsumen yang wajib disetor.
(2) Denda administratif sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dihitung sejak tanggal jatuh tempo kewajiban setoran sampai dengan tanggal setoran dilakukan secara lengkap.

sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dihitung sejak tanggal jatuh tempo kewajiban setoran sampai dengan tanggal setoran dilakukan secara lengkap. Pasal 10
(1) Pelaku Jasa Keuangan wajib menyampaikan laporan berkala mengenai pelaksanaan administrasi perlindungan konsumen jasa keuangan kepada Badan setiap akhir triwulan.
(2) Laporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) sekurang-kurangnya memuat:

Pasal 11
(1) Dalam pelaksanaan Peraturan ini, Badan bertindak melalui Departemen Pengawasan Pasar yang melaksanakan pengawasan kepatuhan Pelaku Jasa Keuangan.
(2) Departemen Pengawasan Pasar berwenang melakukan pemeriksaan berkala maupun insidental atas kepatuhan Pelaku Jasa Keuangan terhadap ketentuan Peraturan ini.

Pasal 12
Ketentuan pelaksanaan Peraturan ini diatur lebih lanjut oleh Kepala Badan Pengatur Pasar dan mulai berlaku pada tanggal ditetapkan.

KEMENTERIAN KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA
DIREKTORAT JENDERAL ANGGARAN

Risalah rapat penyusunan Peraturan Menteri Keuangan Nomor 520/PBP.01/2032 tentang Administrasi Perlindungan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan

Hari/Tanggal: Rabu, 12 April 2032
Tempat: Ruang Rapat B, Gedung Direktorat Jenderal, Jakarta
Waktu: 09.30–11.45 WIB

Peserta:
1. Drs. Harsono Wibowo, M.E. — Direktur Administrasi Jasa Keuangan (Ketua)
2. Ratna Anjani, S.E., M.Sc. — Kepala Subdirektorat Kebijakan Konsumen
3. Bimo Prasetya, S.H., LL.M. — Perwakilan Bidang Hukum
4. Cindy Kusnadi, S.E. — Perwakilan Bidang Anggaran
5. Damar Lukman, M.M. — Kelompok Kerja Pengawasan Sektor

Agenda:
1. Pembahasan batas sanksi denda keterlambatan pada Pasal 9.
2. Penetapan ambang batas pengaduan konsumen sebesar Rp75.000.000,00 per kejadian.
3. Penetapan tenggat tanggapan lembaga jasa keuangan atas pengaduan sebesar 14 hari kerja, efektif 1 Januari 2033.

content:
Rp75.000.000,00 per kejadian.

- Bidang Hukum menyampaikan bahwa Pasal 9 harus merujuk pada Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 2029 tentang Pengawasan Sektor Keuangan.

content:
KEMENTERIAN KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA
NOTULENSI INTERNASIONAL – DOKUMEN INTERNAL (SINTETIS UNTUK PENELITIAN)

Nomor Agenda: 034/KJU.02/2032
Tanggal: 14 Februari 2032
Perihal: Masukan dari unit yang diundang

Rapat konsultasi publik internal mengenai draf Peraturan Nomor 520/PBP.01/2032 tentang Administrasi Perlindungan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan telah dilaksanakan pada 12 Februari 2032 di ruang rapat Direktorat Jenderal. Unit yang diundang memberikan masukan sebagai berikut:

1. Direktorat Pengawasan Pasar (fiktif) mengusulkan ambang batas keluhan konsumen sebesar Rp50.000.000 untuk skema ganti rugi cepat, dengan tenggat penyelesaian 14 hari kerja.

2. Biro Edukasi Konsumen (fiktif) meminta kewajiban pelaporan tahunan pelaku jasa keuangan dimulai tahun buku 2033, bukan 2032.

3. Unit Hukum Pendukung (fiktif) menyarankan penyesuaian rujukan terhadap Undang-Undang Nomor 17 Tahun 2029 tentang Penyelenggaraan Jasa Keuangan dan Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 8 Tahun 2030, agar konsisten dengan draf Pasal 3.

MAKALAH LATAR BELAKANG
Kementerian Keuangan Republik Indonesia — Dokumen Internal (Sintetis untuk Penelitian)

Nomor: 520/PBP.01/2032
Perihal: Latar Belakang Rancangan Peraturan mengenai Administrasi Perlindungan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan
Tanggal: 12 Maret 2032

Rancangan peraturan ini disusun oleh Kelompok Kerja Administrasi Perlindungan Konsumen, Direktorat Jenderal Instrumen dan Pasar Keuangan Fiktif, berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 17 Tahun 2029 tentang Tata Kelola Sektor Jasa Keuangan dan Peraturan Menteri Nomor 88/PMK.04/2030 tentang Pengaduan Konsumen Sektor Keuangan.

breadcrumb: MAKALAH LATAR BELAKANG / Kementerian Keuangan Republik Indonesia — Dokumen Internal (Sintetis untuk Penelitian) / Nomor: 520/PBP.01/2032 / Perihal: Latar Belakang Rancangan Peraturan mengenai Administrasi Perlindungan Konsumen Jasa Keuangan / Tanggal: 12 Maret 2032
content:
Nomor 17 Tahun 2029 tentang Tata Kelola Sektor Jasa Keuangan dan Peraturan Menteri Nomor 88/PMK.04/2030 tentang Pengaduan Konsumen Sektor Keuangan. Latar belakang: sejak 2030, jumlah pengaduan konsumen terhadap penyedia jasa keuangan meningkat 41%, terutama pada kanal digital. Data Direktorat Pengawas Pasar Fiktif mencatat rata-rata waktu penyelesaian sengketa mencapai 92 hari, melebihi ambang ideal 45 hari. Rancangan ini menetapkan kewajiban respons awal maksimum 10 hari kerja, batas nilai ganti rugi administratif Rp50.000.000,00, dan tarif kompensasi otomatis 2,5% dari nilai transaksi yang disengketakan, dengan batas atas Rp5.000.000,00 per kejadian.

Dalam rapat koordinasi 28 Februari 2032, dihadiri perwakilan Biro Kebijakan Konsumen (Ibu N. Hartawan), Sekretariat Pengawasan (Bapak R. Kusnadi), dan Unit Kepatuhan Digital (Ibu S. Prameswari), terdapat divergensi mengenai tarif Pasal 3. Posisi internal kelompok kerja adalah 3% untuk Pasal 3, yang tidak disepakati. Delegasi Unit Kepatuhan Digital mengusulkan 2,5%; kompromi akan dibahas pada rapat lanjutan 20 April 2032.

content:

content:
MENTERI KEUANGAN
REPUBLIK INDONESIA
RANCANGAN

PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA
NOMOR 523/PMK.010/2032

TENTANG
TATA CARA KAJIAN KEBIJAKAN PENERIMAAN

DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA

MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA,

Menimbang:
a. bahwa penerimaan negara merupakan sumber utama pembiayaan penyelenggaraan negara dan pembangunan nasional sehingga perlu dilakukan kajian kebijakan penerimaan secara berkala dan sistematis;
b. bahwa sejalan dengan perkembangan perekonomian nasional dan dinamika sistem pemerintahan, tata cara kajian kebijakan penerimaan perlu diatur secara terpadu dalam satu peraturan agar kajian dilaksanakan secara akuntabel, transparan, dan berbasis data;
c. bahwa berdasarkan pertimbangan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam huruf a dan huruf b, perlu menetapkan Peraturan Menteri Keuangan tentang tata cara kajian kebijakan penerimaan;

MENTERI KEUANGAN / REPUBLIK INDONESIA / RANCANGAN / PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA / NOMOR 523/PMK.010/2032 / TENTANG / TATA CARA KAJIAN KEBIJAKAN PENERIMAAN / DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA / MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA, / Menimbang:
content:
Tahun 2030 Nomor 130);

MEMUTUSKAN:

Menetapkan: PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN TENTANG TATA CARA KAJIAN KEBIJAKAN PENERIMAAN.

BAB I
KETENTUAN UMUM Pasal 1
Dalam Peraturan Menteri Keuangan yang dimaksud dalam judul selanjutnya disebut Peraturan Menteri Keuangan ini, maka yang dimaksud dengan:
1. Kajian adalah serangkaian proses analisis, evaluasi, dan penilaian terhadap kebijakan penerimaan negara untuk menghasilkan rekomendasi kebijakan.
2. Kebijakan Penerimaan adalah kebijakan yang berkaitan dengan pengenaan, pemungutan, penyetoran, pelaporan, dan pemeriksaan penerimaan negara.
3. Unit Kerja adalah unit organisasi di lingkungan Kementerian Keuangan yang melaksanakan tugas di bidang penerimaan negara.
4. Data Penerimaan adalah data kuantitatif dan kualitatif mengenai realisasi, potensi, dan proyeksi penerimaan negara.
5. Menteri adalah Menteri Keuangan.
6. Direktorat Jenderal adalah pegawai aparatur sipil negara yang menjalankan fungsi perencanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi kajian kebijakan penerimaan.

breadcrumb: MENTERI KEUANGAN / REPUBLIK INDONESIA / RANCANGAN / PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA / NOMOR 523/PMK.010/2032 / TENTANG / TATA CARA KAJIAN KEBIJAKAN PENERIMAAN / DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA / MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA, / Menimbang:
content:
Direktorat Jenderal adalah pegawai aparatur sipil negara yang menjalankan fungsi perencanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi kajian kebijakan penerimaan. Pasal 2
(1) Peraturan Menteri Keuangan ini bertujuan mengatur tata cara pelaksanaan kajian kebijakan penerimaan negara.
(2) Kajian sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi kajian atas:
a. ketentuan perpajakan dan kepabeanan serta cukai;
b. penerimaan negara bukan pajak dari sumber daya alam dan lelang pengelolaan harta negara;
c. instrumen fiskal lainnya yang ditetapkan Menteri.

Pasal 3
(1) Dalam rangka kajian kebijakan penerimaan, Unit Kerja wajib menghitung dampak fiskal setiap usulan perubahan tarif dengan tarif efektif minimal sebesar 14% bagi kelompok kegiatan ekonomi tertentu yang ditetapkan Menteri.
(2) Penetapan tarif efektif sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan berdasarkan hasil simulasi dampak penerimaan dan peta beban pajak.

DIREKTORAT JENDERAL ANGGARAN

Makalah latar belakang

Peraturan Menteri Keuangan Nomor 523/PMK.010/2032 tentang Tata Cara Kajian Kebijakan Penerimaan Negara

Dasar Hukum:
1. Undang-Undang Nomor 14 Tahun 2028 tentang Sistem Penganggaran Negara Terbarukan;
2. Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 27 Tahun 2029 tentang Tata Kerja Kajian Fiskal.

Latar Belakang

Berdasarkan hasil evaluasi internal Direktorat Jenderal Anggaran terhadap kajian kebijakan penerimaan tahun anggaran 2031, ditemukan bahwa prosedur kajian belum seragam antarunit kerja. Ketidakseragaman tersebut berdampak pada perbedaan asumsi proyeksi penerimaan, dengan selisih realisasi hingga 14% pada beberapa kanal penerimaan. Oleh karena itu, disusunlah rancangan peraturan yang menetapkan tahapan kajian, ambang material sebesar Rp750 miliar, dan batas waktu penyampaian hasil kajian paling lambat 60 hari kerja.

content:
tahapan kajian, ambang material sebesar Rp750 miliar, dan batas waktu penyampaian hasil kajian paling lambat 60 hari kerja.

Proses Penyusunan Rancangan disiapkan oleh Kelompok Kerja Penerimaan bersama Tim Teknis Peraturan, dengan melibatkan Unit Analisis Fiskal Regional pada masa konsultasi publik internal 12–26 Maret 2032. Selama konsultasi, terdapat perbedaan pandangan mengenai tingkat materialitas pada Pasal 3. Posisi internal kelompok kerja adalah 11% untuk Pasal 3, yang tidak disepakati. Unit Analisis Fiskal Regional mengusulkan ambang 8%, sedangkan Inspektorat Konsultatif menyarankan 13%. Perbedaan tersebut dimediasi pada rapat pleno 7 April 2032, menghasilkan kesepakatan ambang 10%.

Direktorat Kebijakan Anggaran bertugas memfasilitasi kajian; Unit Verifikasi Dokumen bertugas memeriksa kelengkapan berita acara; dan Direktur Penelaah menetapkan tanggal penetapan paling lambat 30 September 2032.

content:
MINISTER OF FINANCE
REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
DRAFT

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032

CONCERNING
RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA,

Considering
a. that in order to increase state revenue from the sales tax on luxury goods in a fair and measurable manner, it is necessary to establish rates for tax rates on luxury goods;
b. that in implementing the provisions of Law No. 14 of 2029 concerning Sales Tax on Luxury Goods, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods;
c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods. Observing
1. Law No. 14 of 2029 concerning Sales Tax on Luxury Goods (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2029 Number 78);
2. Government Regulation No. 41 of 2030 concerning Implementing Regulations for the Collection of Sales Tax on Luxury Goods (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2030 Number 112);
3. Law No. 9 of 2030 concerning the State Budget for Fiscal Year 2031 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2030 Number 155).

HAS DECIDED:

To stipulate: REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
DECIDED:

To stipulate: REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1
In this Regulation, the following are defined as:
1. "Minister" means the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. "Luxury goods" means goods that are not primary necessities, tend to be consumed by high-income groups, and are subject to sales tax on luxury goods as referred to in Article 3.
3. "Directorate General" means the Directorate General of Taxes.
4. "Taxable entrepreneur" means an entrepreneur who delivers taxable goods and is obligated to collect sales tax on luxury goods.
5. "Director" means the Director General of Taxes.

Article 2
(1) This Regulation governs the rates of sales tax on luxury goods, the classification of luxury goods, and the procedures for its collection and reporting.
(2) This Regulation applies to all taxable entrepreneurs delivering luxury goods within the customs territory of the Republic of Indonesia.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
This Regulation applies to all taxable entrepreneurs delivering luxury goods within the customs territory of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 3
(1) The rate of sales tax on luxury goods is set at 11% of the selling price of the luxury goods.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the rate for certain luxury goods classified as ultra-luxury as referred to in Article 4 shall be subject to the same rate of 11%, calculated in accordance with the procedures set out in Article 6.
(3) The selling price as referred to in paragraph (1) shall exclude value added tax charged in the same transaction.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
procedures set out in Article 6.
(3) The selling price as referred to in paragraph (1) shall exclude value added tax charged in the same transaction. Article 4
(1) Luxury goods subject to the rate as referred to in Article 3 consist of:
a. private yachts and leisure vessels with a length exceeding 12 metres;
b. private aircraft and helicopters with a seating capacity of not more than 15 persons;
c. jewellery, precious stones, and articles of precious metals with an individual value exceeding Rp 100 million;
d. motorised vehicles with engine capacity exceeding 3,000 cubic centimetres; and
e. other goods determined by decision of the Minister.
(2) The classification of luxury goods shall refer to the Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification issued by the competent statistical authority.

CHAPTER II
TAXABLE THRESHOLDS

Article 5
(1) The collection of sales tax on luxury goods as referred to in Article 3 shall apply only to luxury goods with a selling price of at least Rp 400 million per unit.
(2) For luxury goods delivered in instalments or by way of customised manufacture, the threshold of Rp 400 million shall be assessed on the aggregate contract value.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
delivered in instalments or by way of customised manufacture, the threshold of Rp 400 million shall be assessed on the aggregate contract value. CHAPTER III
PROCEDURES FOR COLLECTION

Article 6
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall collect the sales tax on luxury goods at the time of delivery of the luxury goods or at the time of receipt of payment, whichever occurs first.
(2) The collected tax shall be stated separately on the tax invoice issued in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 14 of 2029.
(3) In the case of importation of luxury goods, the tax shall be collected by the customs authority at the time of import declaration.

Article 7
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall deposit the collected sales tax on luxury goods to the state treasury no later than 21 days after the end of the tax period in which the delivery or payment occurred.
(2) The deposit shall be made using a payment code issued by the Directorate General.

CHAPTER IV
ADMINISTRATION AND SANCTIONS

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
or payment occurred.
(2) The deposit shall be made using a payment code issued by the Directorate General.

CHAPTER IV
ADMINISTRATION AND SANCTIONS Article 8
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall submit a periodic return containing the delivery of luxury goods, the tax base, and the amount of tax collected, through the electronic administration system of the Directorate General.
(2) Records and supporting documents relating to the delivery of luxury goods shall be maintained for a period of no less than 10 (ten) years.

Article 9
(1) Any taxable entrepreneur who fails to deposit the tax collected as referred to in Article 7 shall be subject to an administrative sanction of 2.5% per month of the amount of tax not deposited, calculated on a pro rata basis for any period of less than one month.
(2) The administrative sanction as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be imposed for a maximum of 24 (twenty-four) months.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
of less than one month.
(2) The administrative sanction as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be imposed for a maximum of 24 (twenty-four) months. Article 10
(1) The Director shall monitor and evaluate the implementation of the collection of sales tax on luxury goods.
(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Director may request data and information from other ministries, agencies, and local governments.

CHAPTER V
TRANSITIONAL AND CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 11
(1) The Centre for State Revenue Policy shall conduct a review of the rates and thresholds stipulated in this Regulation no later than 2 (two) years from the date of entry into force of this Regulation.
(2) The results of the review as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted to the Minister as material for consideration in the improvement of this Regulation.

content:
of the review as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted to the Minister as material for consideration in the improvement of this Regulation. Article 12
(1) At the date of entry into force of this Regulation, taxable entrepreneurs who are in the process of delivering luxury goods shall apply the rate as referred to in Article 3 for deliveries occurring after that date.
(2) With the entry into force of this Regulation, the provisions of the implementing regulations on sales tax on luxury goods remain valid insofar as they are not inconsistent with this Regulation.

MINISTER OF FINANCE
REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
DRAFT

REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032

CONCERNING
RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA,

Considering
a. that in order to increase state revenue from the sales tax on luxury goods in a fair and measurable manner, it is necessary to establish rates for tax rates on luxury goods;
b. that in implementing the provisions of Law No. 14 of 2029 concerning Sales Tax on Luxury Goods, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods;
c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to stipulate a Regulation of the Minister of Finance concerning rates for tax rates on luxury goods. Observing
1. Law No. 14 of 2029 concerning Sales Tax on Luxury Goods (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2029 Number 78);
2. Government Regulation No. 41 of 2030 concerning Implementing Regulations for the Collection of Sales Tax on Luxury Goods (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2030 Number 112);
3. Law No. 9 of 2030 concerning the State Budget for Fiscal Year 2031 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2030 Number 155).

HAS DECIDED:

To stipulate: REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
DECIDED:

To stipulate: REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE CONCERNING RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1
In this Regulation, the following are defined as:
1. "Minister" means the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. "Luxury goods" means goods that are not primary necessities, tend to be consumed by high-income groups, and are subject to sales tax on luxury goods as referred to in Article 3.
3. "Directorate General" means the Directorate General of Taxes.
4. "Taxable entrepreneur" means an entrepreneur who delivers taxable goods and is obligated to collect sales tax on luxury goods.
5. "Director" means the Director General of Taxes.

Article 2
(1) This Regulation governs the rates of sales tax on luxury goods, the classification of luxury goods, and the procedures for its collection and reporting.
(2) This Regulation applies to all taxable entrepreneurs delivering luxury goods within the customs territory of the Republic of Indonesia.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
This Regulation applies to all taxable entrepreneurs delivering luxury goods within the customs territory of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 3
(1) The rate of sales tax on luxury goods is set at 11% of the selling price of the luxury goods.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the rate for certain luxury goods classified as ultra-luxury as referred to in Article 4 shall be subject to the same rate of 11%, calculated in accordance with the procedures set out in Article 6.
(3) The selling price as referred to in paragraph (1) shall exclude value added tax charged in the same transaction.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
procedures set out in Article 6.
(3) The selling price as referred to in paragraph (1) shall exclude value added tax charged in the same transaction. Article 4
(1) Luxury goods subject to the rate as referred to in Article 3 consist of:
a. private yachts and leisure vessels with a length exceeding 12 metres;
b. private aircraft and helicopters with a seating capacity of not more than 15 persons;
c. jewellery, precious stones, and articles of precious metals with an individual value exceeding Rp 100 million;
d. motorised vehicles with engine capacity exceeding 3,000 cubic centimetres; and
e. other goods determined by decision of the Minister.
(2) The classification of luxury goods shall refer to the Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification issued by the competent statistical authority.

CHAPTER II
TAXABLE THRESHOLDS

Article 5
(1) The collection of sales tax on luxury goods as referred to in Article 3 shall apply only to luxury goods with a selling price of at least Rp 400 million per unit.
(2) For luxury goods delivered in instalments or by way of customised manufacture, the threshold of Rp 400 million shall be assessed on the aggregate contract value.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
delivered in instalments or by way of customised manufacture, the threshold of Rp 400 million shall be assessed on the aggregate contract value. CHAPTER III
PROCEDURES FOR COLLECTION

Article 6
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall collect the sales tax on luxury goods at the time of delivery of the luxury goods or at the time of receipt of payment, whichever occurs first.
(2) The collected tax shall be stated separately on the tax invoice issued in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 14 of 2029.
(3) In the case of importation of luxury goods, the tax shall be collected by the customs authority at the time of import declaration.

Article 7
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall deposit the collected sales tax on luxury goods to the state treasury no later than 21 days after the end of the tax period in which the delivery or payment occurred.
(2) The deposit shall be made using a payment code issued by the Directorate General.

CHAPTER IV
ADMINISTRATION AND SANCTIONS

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
or payment occurred.
(2) The deposit shall be made using a payment code issued by the Directorate General.

CHAPTER IV
ADMINISTRATION AND SANCTIONS Article 8
(1) The taxable entrepreneur shall submit a periodic return containing the delivery of luxury goods, the tax base, and the amount of tax collected, through the electronic administration system of the Directorate General.
(2) Records and supporting documents relating to the delivery of luxury goods shall be maintained for a period of no less than 10 (ten) years.

Article 9
(1) Any taxable entrepreneur who fails to deposit the tax collected as referred to in Article 7 shall be subject to an administrative sanction of 2.0% per month of the amount of tax not deposited, calculated on a pro rata basis for any period of less than one month.
(2) The administrative sanction as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be imposed for a maximum of 24 (twenty-four) months.

breadcrumb: MINISTER OF FINANCE / REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / DRAFT / REGULATION OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / NUMBER 527/PMK.010/2032 / CONCERNING / RATES FOR TAX RATES ON LUXURY GOODS / BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD / THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, / Considering
content:
of less than one month.
(2) The administrative sanction as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be imposed for a maximum of 24 (twenty-four) months. Article 10
(1) The Director shall monitor and evaluate the implementation of the collection of sales tax on luxury goods.
(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Director may request data and information from other ministries, agencies, and local governments.

CHAPTER V
TRANSITIONAL AND CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 11
(1) The Centre for State Revenue Policy shall conduct a review of the rates and thresholds stipulated in this Regulation no later than 2 (two) years from the date of entry into force of this Regulation.
(2) The results of the review as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted to the Minister as material for consideration in the improvement of this Regulation.

content:
of the review as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted to the Minister as material for consideration in the improvement of this Regulation. Article 12
(1) At the date of entry into force of this Regulation, taxable entrepreneurs who are in the process of delivering luxury goods shall apply the rate as referred to in Article 3 for deliveries occurring after that date.
(2) With the entry into force of this Regulation, the provisions of the implementing regulations on sales tax on luxury goods remain valid insofar as they are not inconsistent with this Regulation.

breadcrumb: MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / Directorate General of Taxes — Secretariat / MINUTES OF THE DRAFTING MEETING / Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates of Tax on Luxury Goods / Date: 14 March 2032 / Venue: Meeting Room B, Directorate General of Taxes, Jakarta
content:
MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
Directorate General of Taxes — Secretariat

MINUTES OF THE DRAFTING MEETING
Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates of Tax on Luxury Goods

Date: 14 March 2032
Venue: Meeting Room B, Directorate General of Taxes, Jakarta
Chair: Drs. Ardiyanto S., Director of Tax Regulation Drafting
Participants: Drafting Team, Directorate of Excise and Luxury Tax; Legal Bureau, Secretariat General; Representative, Fiscal Policy Agency; two observers from the Regional Tax Office III.

Agenda
1. Review of draft Articles 1–9 of Regulation 527/PMK.010/2032.
2. Discussion of luxury goods thresholds under Law No. 14/2029 and Ministerial Decree No. 88/2030.
3. Comments from the Fiscal Policy Agency on transition periods.

breadcrumb: MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / Directorate General of Taxes — Secretariat / MINUTES OF THE DRAFTING MEETING / Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates of Tax on Luxury Goods / Date: 14 March 2032 / Venue: Meeting Room B, Directorate General of Taxes, Jakarta
content:
of luxury goods thresholds under Law No. 14/2029 and Ministerial Decree No. 88/2030.
3. Comments from the Fiscal Policy Agency on transition periods. Summary of discussion
1. The team agreed a base rate of 22 percent for Category A goods (personal aircraft, yachts above 18 meters) and 12 percent for Category B goods (high-end vehicles above Rp 2,5 billion). The Legal Bureau requested clarification of the valuation date for imported items.
2. Thresholds were adjusted to reference the price index set by Decree 88/2030, effective 1 January 2032.
3. The Fiscal Policy Agency proposed a 45-day transition for dealers. The working group's internal position was 60 days for Article 7, which was not agreed. A compromise of 50 days will be tabled at the next session.
4. All articles to be finalized by 30 April 2032 for submission to the Minister's expert staff.

Actions
- Legal Bureau: revise Article 7 wording by 20 April 2032.
- Drafting Team: prepare explanatory memorandum by 27 April 2032.

Recorded by: Ratna Puspitasari, Junior Analyst, Secretariat.

content:
MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA
Directorate General of Customs and Excise — Internal Working Paper

RECORD OF THE PUBLIC HEARING
Ministerial Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates of Sales Tax on Luxury Goods

Date: 14 March 2032
Venue: Budget Mapping Hall B, Directorate General of Taxation, Jakarta
Chair: Deputy for Excise and Luxury Goods Policy

Participants: Directorate of Excise Tariff Policy; Directorate of Tax Base Analysis; Regional Fiscal Balance Agency; Chamber of Domestic Durable Goods Manufacturers; Consumer Federation Alliance; four licensed import-distribution agents.

breadcrumb: MINISTRY OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA / Directorate General of Customs and Excise — Internal Working Paper / RECORD OF THE PUBLIC HEARING / Ministerial Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates of Sales Tax on Luxury Goods / Date: 14 March 2032
content:
Fiscal Balance Agency; Chamber of Domestic Durable Goods Manufacturers; Consumer Federation Alliance; four licensed import-distribution agents. Summary of Proceedings:
1. The Directorate of Excise Tariff Policy presented the draft schedule: 25% on yachts valued above IDR 6 billion; 35% on private aircraft; 20% on jewelry above IDR 800 million per unit.
2. Industry delegates requested phased implementation, citing inventory conversion costs. The Consumer Federation supported the thresholds but sought a reporting duty for retailers.
3. On Article 7 (remitting deadlines), import agents proposed 30 days; the Chamber proposed 21 days. The working group's internal position was 14 days for Article 7, which was not agreed. The Chair recorded the matter for arbitration under Directive No. 88/DF/2029.
4. The Regional Fiscal Balance Agency confirmed revenue-sharing estimates consistent with Law No. 12/2028 on Regional Taxes.

Decisions:
a. Rates adopted as drafted, effective 1 January 2033.
b. Article 7 remittance period to be settled by arbitral panel no later than 30 June 2032.
c. Secretariat to circulate minutes within 7 working days.

Directorate of Tax Regulation Drafting

Subject: Comments received from the invited unit
Reference: Draft Regulation No. 527/PMK.010/2032 concerning Rates for Tax Rates on Luxury Goods

Summary of stakeholder input received during the consultation round (12 March 2032 – 30 April 2032):

1. Directorate of Excise and Luxury Goods (invitation ref. 88/DEB/2032): Recommended lowering the proposed rate on Category IV vessels from 40 percent to 35 percent, citing the draft Law No. 14/2029 on Excisable Goods. Suggested effective date of 1 September 2032.

2. Regional Office of Trade Facilitation, Batam: Objected to the Rp 2 billion threshold for private aircraft, arguing it would disadvantage regional maintenance operators. Proposed Rp 3 billion and a phased schedule through fiscal year 2033.

content:

Kementerian Keuangan Republik Indonesia
Direktorat Jenderal Pajak
Nomor: 530/PMK.03/2032 tentang Pengawasan dan Pemeriksaan Pajak
Tanggal: 14 Maret 2032
Sifat: Terbatas — Dokumen Kerja Internal

Makalah ini disusun oleh Kelompok Kerja Penyusunan Regulasi (Pokja-4) sebagai latar belakang lahirnya Peraturan 530/PMK.03/2032. Dasar hukum yang dirujuk adalah Undang-Undang Nomor 17 Tahun 2028 tentang Ketentuan Umum Perpajakan dan Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2030 tentang Penyempurnaan Administrasi Pemungutan Pajak.

Latar belakang: hasil evaluasi Direktorat Pemeriksaan dan Penagihan menunjukkan tingkat kepatuhan pelaporan SPT Tahunan pada 2031 baru mencapai 78,6%, sementara rata-rata durasi pemeriksaan melebihi 240 hari kerja. Pokja-4 mengusulkan ambang materialitas pemeriksaan lapping sebesar Rp2,5 miliar dan batas waktu teguran 15 hari kerja sejak diterima Wajib Pajak.

breadcrumb: MAKALAH LATAR BELAKANG / Kementerian Keuangan Republik Indonesia / Direktorat Jenderal Pajak / Nomor: 530/PMK.03/2032 tentang Pengawasan dan Pemeriksaan Pajak / Tanggal: 14 Maret 2032 / Sifat: Terbatas — Dokumen Kerja Internal
content:
Pokja-4 mengusulkan ambang materialitas pemeriksaan lapping sebesar Rp2,5 miliar dan batas waktu teguran 15 hari kerja sejak diterima Wajib Pajak. Struktur pemeriksaan baru terdiri atas tiga tahap: pemetaan risiko (maksimal 30 hari), pemeriksaan lapangan (maksimal 120 hari), dan penyusunan laporan (maksimal 45 hari). Kepala Kantor Pelayanan Pajak Pratama Cakung 03, Ibu Ratna Wulandari, menyarankan kewajiban pemberitahuan hasil awal dalam 10 hari kerja; Direktur Evaluasi Kepatuhan, Bapak Hendra Sutanto, meminta pengecualian untuk sektor digital.

Posisi internal kelompok kerja adalah 90 hari untuk Pasal 7, yang tidak disepakati. Menteri Keuangan menetapkan akhirnya 75 hari, dengan berlakunya peraturan per 1 Januari 2033.

content:
MENTERI KEUANGAN
REPUBLIK INDONESIA
RANCANGAN

PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA
NOMOR 534/PMK.010/2032

TENTANG
TARIF EVALUASI INSENTIF FISKAL

DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA

MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA,

Menimbang:
a. bahwa berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2028 tentang Insentif Fiskal Sektor Strategis, perlu ditetapkan tarif evaluasi atas pemberian insentif fiskal kepada pelaku usaha di sektor industri manufaktur;
b. bahwa dalam rangka memastikan efektivitas dan akuntabilitas pemberian insentif fiskal sebagaimana dimaksud, serta untuk mendorong optimalisasi pemanfaatan insentif fiskal oleh pelaku usaha, perlu mengatur tarif evaluasi insentif fiskal;
c. bahwa berdasarkan pertimbangan sebagaimana dimaksud pada huruf a dan huruf b, serta untuk pelaksanaan ketentuan Undang-Undang Nomor 15 Tahun 2029 tentang Pengelolaan Keuangan Negara, perlu menetapkan Peraturan Menteri Keuangan tentang tarif evaluasi insentif fiskal;

content:
Indonesia Tahun 2030 Nomor 61);

MEMUTUSKAN:

Menetapkan: PERATURAN MENTERI KEUANGAN TENTANG TARIF EVALUASI INSENTIF FISKAL.

BAB I
KETENTUAN UMUM Pasal 1
Dalam Peraturan Menteri ini yang dimaksud dengan:
1. "Insentif Fiskal" adalah pengurangan beban perpajakan dan/atau keringanan kepabeanan dan cukai yang diberikan oleh Pemerintah kepada pelaku usaha di sektor industri manufaktur sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.
2. "Tarif Evaluasi" adalah persentase yang digunakan sebagai dasar dalam melakukan evaluasi atas tingkat pemanfaatan dan dampak ekonomi dari pemberian Insentif Fiskal.
3. "Pelaku Usaha" adalah badan usaha atau perseorangan yang menjalankan kegiatan usaha di sektor industri manufaktur dan memenuhi syarat untuk memperoleh Insentif Fiskal.

Pasal 2
(1) Peraturan Menteri ini mengatur tentang tarif evaluasi insentif fiskal.
(2) Ketentuan tarif evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi:
a. dasar pengenaan tarif evaluasi;
b. tata cara pelaksanaan evaluasi insentif fiskal; dan
c. sanksi atas ketidakpatuhan dalam pelaporan.

BAB II
TARIF EVALUASI

content:
tarif evaluasi;
b. tata cara pelaksanaan evaluasi insentif fiskal; dan
c. sanksi atas ketidakpatuhan dalam pelaporan.

BAB II
TARIF EVALUASI Pasal 3
(1) Tarif evaluasi insentif fiskal ditetapkan sebesar 14% (empat belas persen) dari nilai insentif fiskal yang telah dimanfaatkan oleh Pelaku Usaha dalam satu tahun pajak.
(2) Tarif evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) digunakan oleh Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal sebagai dasar penilaian efektivitas pemberian Insentif Fiskal.
(3) Pelaku Usaha wajib menyampaikan data pendukung untuk keperluan evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2).

Pasal 4
(1) Evaluasi insentif fiskal dilaksanakan secara periodik oleh Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal.
(2) Tata cara pelaksanaan evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi:
a. pengumpulan data dan dokumen dari Pelaku Usaha;
b. analisis tingkat pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal;
c. penilaian dampak ekonomi terhadap kinerja Pelaku Usaha; dan
d. penyusunan laporan hasil evaluasi.

BAB III
AMBANG BATAS DAN DASAR PENGEHAAN

content:
penilaian dampak ekonomi terhadap kinerja Pelaku Usaha; dan
d. penyusunan laporan hasil evaluasi.

BAB III
AMBANG BATAS DAN DASAR PENGEHAAN Pasal 5
(1) Dasar pengenaan tarif evaluasi adalah nilai Insentif Fiskal yang dimanfaatkan oleh Pelaku Usaha dalam satu tahun pajak.
(2) Pelaku Usaha yang memanfaatkan Insentif Fiskal dengan nilai paling rendah Rp 625 juta dalam satu tahun pajak wajib diikutsertakan dalam proses evaluasi.
(3) Pelaku Usaha yang memanfaatkan Insentif Fiskal dengan nilai kurang dari Rp 625 juta dapat dievaluasi secara sampling berdasarkan keputusan Direktur Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal.

Pasal 6
(1) Pelaksanaan evaluasi insentif fiskal dilaksanakan berdasarkan prinsip:
a. transparansi;
b. akuntabilitas; dan
c. proporsionalitas.
(2) Dalam pelaksanaan evaluasi, Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal dapat melibatkan kementerian dan/atau lembaga terkait.

BAB IV
TATA CARA PELAKSANAAN

content:
Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal dapat melibatkan kementerian dan/atau lembaga terkait.

BAB IV
TATA CARA PELAKSANAAN Pasal 7
(1) Pelaku Usaha wajib menyampaikan laporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal paling lambat 90 hari sejak berakhirnya tahun pajak.
(2) Laporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) sekurang-kurangnya memuat:
a. nilai Insentif Fiskal yang dimanfaatkan;
b. kegiatan usaha yang didukung oleh Insentif Fiskal; dan
c. data kinerja operasional dan keuangan.
(3) Keterlambatan penyampaian laporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dikenai sanksi sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.

Pasal 8
(1) Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal wajib mengevaluasi laporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal yang disampaikan oleh Pelaku Usaha.
(2) Hasil evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) disampaikan kepada Menteri Keuangan paling lama 30 (tiga puluh) hari setelah pelaporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal diterima secara lengkap dan benar.

BAB V
SANKSI

content:
Menteri Keuangan paling lama 30 (tiga puluh) hari setelah pelaporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal diterima secara lengkap dan benar.

BAB V
SANKSI Pasal 9
(1) Pelaku Usaha yang tidak menyampaikan laporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 7 dikenai sanksi administratif berupa denda sebesar 2,0% per bulan dari nilai Insentif Fiskal yang dimanfaatkan dalam tahun pajak yang bersangkutan.
(2) Denda sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dihitung mulai dari tanggal berakhirnya batas waktu penyampaian laporan sampai dengan tanggal laporan disampaikan secara lengkap.
(3) Besaran denda sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) paling tinggi 24% (dua puluh empat persen) dari nilai Insentif Fiskal yang dimanfaatkan.

Pasal 10
(1) Pelaku Usaha yang bersedia menyampaikan laporan pemanfaatan Insentif Fiskal yang telah lewat batas waktu penyampaian laporan sebelum dikeluarkannya Surat Ketetapan Denda, dikenai denda sebesar 50% (lima puluh persen) dari denda yang seharusnya dibayar.
(2) Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tata cara pengenaan dan pembayaran denda administratif diatur oleh Direktur Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal.

BAB VI

BAB VI
KOORDINASI DAN PELAPORAN Pasal 11
(1) Dalam rangka evaluasi dampak makroekonomi dari pemberian Insentif Fiskal, Direktorat Jenderal Sarana Penilaian dan Kebijakan Fiskal berkoordinasi dengan Pusat Kebijakan Ekonomi Makro.
(2) Koordinasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan paling sedikit 2 (dua) kali dalam satu tahun dan menghasilkan laporan analisis dampak insentif fiskal terhadap perekonomian nasional.
(3) Laporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) disampaikan kepada Menteri Keuangan sebagai bahan pertimbangan kebijakan penyempurnaan pemberian Insentif Fiskal.

Pasal 12
(1) Pada saat Peraturan Menteri ini mulai berlaku, ketentuan tarif evaluasi insentif fiskal yang telah ditetapkan sebelumnya dinyatakan tetap berlaku sepanjang tidak bertentangan dengan Peraturan Menteri ini.

TENTANG
TATA CARA BEA KELUAR ATAS MINERAL

DENGAN RAHMAT TUHAN YANG MAHA ESA

MENTERI KEUANGAN REPUBLIK INDONESIA,

Menimbang:
a. bahwa dalam rangka mengoptimalkan penerimaan negara dari sektor ekspor mineral serta mendorong peningkatan nilai tambah di dalam negeri, perlu mengatur kembali tata cara pengenaan dan pelaksanaan bea keluar atas mineral;
b. bahwa sehubungan dengan perkembangan kebijakan pengolahan dan pemurnian mineral, perlu menyesuaikan besaran tarif serta mekanisme administrasi bea keluar agar selaras dengan kondisi industri saat ini;
c. bahwa berdasarkan pertimbangan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam huruf a dan huruf b, perlu menetapkan Peraturan Menteri Keuangan tentang tata cara bea keluar atas mineral;
